site.intro: 統計課本教你怎麼算，很少告訴你這些東西當初是為了什麼問題被發明出來，又是在哪裡開始被誤用。這個站一次處理一個看起來理所當然、來歷卻可疑的概念：它為什麼長成這樣，是誰為了什麼發明它，以及它壞掉的時候會壞在哪裡。文章裡的模擬都可以親手轉動，因為有些事情得自己按下去重跑一萬次才會相信。

articles.label: 文章
articles.blurb: 一篇處理一個概念，從它的來歷讀到它的誤用。

glossary.label: 術語表
glossary.blurb: 文章裡用到的每個術語，先一句話講定義，再給一個真實發生過的例子，以及它最常在哪裡被讀反。術語在正文中出現時，同一份定義會浮出來，不必離開閱讀。

site.note: 每個例子都查得到出處，出處就掛在句子旁邊；模擬用固定的亂數種子，同樣的按鈕在任何一台機器上跑出同樣的數字。整站中英雙語，右上角切換。

en.intro: Textbooks teach you how to compute. They rarely tell you what problem a method was invented to solve, or where it started being misused. This site takes one such idea at a time — one that looks self-evident and has a questionable history — and asks why it has the shape it has, who built it and for what, and what exactly breaks when it is misapplied. The simulations are yours to turn, because some things you only believe after re-running them ten thousand times yourself.

articles.label: Articles
articles.blurb: One idea per piece, read from where it came from to where it goes wrong.

glossary.label: Glossary
glossary.blurb: Every term the articles lean on: a one-line definition, an example that actually happened, and the way it is usually misread. Where a term appears in the prose, the same definition surfaces in place, so you never have to leave the page to look it up.

en.note: Every example has a source, and the source hangs beside the sentence. The simulations run on fixed seeds, so the same button gives the same numbers on any machine. The whole site is in both languages; the switch is at the top right.

topics.label: 統計推論
topics.blurb: 假設檢定、估計、信賴區間——被用得最多、也被誤解得最深的一塊。

en.label: Inference
en.blurb: Hypothesis tests, estimates, intervals — the most used and the most misread part of the subject.

topics.label: 隨機與收斂
topics.blurb: 一個程序要重複幾次，結果才能當成隨機的——距離怎麼定義，收斂有多快。

en.label: Randomness and convergence
en.blurb: How many times a procedure has to repeat before its output counts as random: how the distance is defined, and how fast it closes.

articles.title: 一副牌要洗幾次才算洗好
articles.subtitle: 同一副撲克牌，換一種距離就換一個答案：五次、七次、十二次
articles.summary: 52 張牌分成兩疊、交錯落下（鴿尾式）洗七次，與均勻分佈的全變異距離是 0.334。這個數字的意思是：拿洗過的牌和電腦排的隨機牌各一副放在你面前，就算用最會挑毛病的方法去檢查，也只有 66.7% 的把握指出哪一副洗過，瞎猜是 50%。改用資訊量衡量，洗五次剩 3.52% 的資訊；只在意紅黑，第六次的分離距離是 0.317；要讓全副牌序在分離距離下收斂，洗十二次仍有 0.278。文內的精確表由本站以整數有理數重算，與 Bayer–Diaconis 1992 年的原表相符。

en.title: How many shuffles does a deck need
en.subtitle: One deck of cards: change the distance and the answer changes to five, seven or twelve
en.summary: Seven riffle shuffles (split the deck in two, let the packets fall interleaved) leave a 52-card deck 0.334 away from uniform in total variation. Put that deck beside one a computer arranged at random: even the shrewdest check anyone can run identifies the shuffled one only 66.7 percent of the time, against 50 percent for a guess. Measured by information, 3.52 percent survives five shuffles; for colours alone the separation distance is 0.317 by the sixth; the full order is still 0.278 away after twelve. The exact table here was recomputed in exact integer arithmetic and agrees with the 1992 original.

articles.title: 大法官站在哪裡：從投票估計理想點
articles.subtitle: 用貝氏分級反應模型把真投票變成一條違憲宣告傾向的軸，檢驗它沿不沿提名總統結構化——一個有紀律的 null，加一層測得到的協作訊號
articles.summary: 把一位大法官放到一條「傾向」的軸上，這條軸從哪裡來？本文以憲法法庭 2022 年後官方逐項立場表為真投票，用 Samejima 分級反應模型的貝氏估計逐法官的違憲宣告傾向，再用置換檢定看它沿不沿提名總統排列。四個維度都測不到效果，而這個 null 帶檢定力、等價與規格曲線的紀律；逐法官可信區間普遍很寬、相鄰全部重疊，這屆在稀疏異議下多半彼此不可區分。另一層用 1949 年以來的意見書共同具名網絡、階層二項模型，測到同提名人中等而穩健的正效果。投票層測不到、協作層測得到，兩層各說各的。台灣既有實證研究沒有一篇用過官方逐項真投票——本文補上這個缺口，並對一篇問題意識高度重疊、迄今未取得全文的研究，在新穎性上保留。

en.title: Where Do the Justices Stand: Estimating Ideal Points from Votes
en.subtitle: A Bayesian graded-response model turns real votes into an axis of tendency to strike down, and a permutation test asks whether it lines up with the nominating president — a disciplined null, plus one collaboration-layer signal that is real
en.summary: Where does the axis come from when we place a justice on a scale of tendency? Using the Taiwan Constitutional Court's official per-item vote records since 2022 as real votes, this piece estimates each justice's tendency to strike down (theta) with a Bayesian graded-response model, then tests whether that axis aligns with the nominating president. Nothing is detectable on four dimensions, and the null carries power, equivalence, and specification-curve discipline; per-justice credible intervals are wide and all adjacent ones overlap, so in this sparse-dissent term the justices are mostly indistinguishable. A second layer, the co-signing network of opinions since 1949 modelled with a hierarchical binomial, does find a moderate and robust same-nominee effect. The voting layer detects nothing; the collaboration layer detects something; the two speak to different things. No prior Taiwanese study has used official per-item real votes — this piece fills that gap, and reserves its novelty claim against one closely overlapping study whose full text remains unavailable.

articles.title: 怎麼證明「沒有差別」
articles.subtitle: 檢定力與等價檢定：把「沒測到差異」變成「差異小到不重要」
articles.summary: 一個檢定跑出 p = 0.56，你不能因此說兩者相同；不顯著可能只是這個研究看不清楚那麼小的差異。本文用學名藥的生體相等性當例子，說明檢定力（研究看得見多大的效果）與等價檢定（TOST：正面證明效果落在一個事先訂好的邊界內），以及為什麼「不顯著」要拆成「能排除任何重要差異」與「只是測不到」兩種。

en.title: How to Show There Is No Difference
en.subtitle: Power and equivalence tests: turning "we found no difference" into "any difference is too small to matter"
en.summary: A test returns p = 0.56, and you cannot conclude the two are the same — a non-significant result may just mean the study had no power to see the difference. This article uses drug bioequivalence to explain statistical power (how large an effect a study can see) and equivalence testing (TOST: bounding the effect inside a margin fixed in advance), and why "not significant" has to be split into "we can rule out any meaningful difference" and "we simply could not tell".

articles.title: 到底什麼是信賴區間
articles.subtitle: 一則民調的「誤差 ±4 個百分點」，和那句 95% 到底掛在誰身上
articles.summary: 民調說某人的支持度是 45%、誤差 ±4 個百分點，於是報紙寫「真實支持度有 95% 的機率落在 41% 到 49% 之間」。這句話幾乎每個人都會講，而它是錯的。這篇從一個平均數把信賴區間親手推一遍，看那句 95% 是怎麼在「代入手上的數字」那一步失去立足點的；再用潛艇、比值區間、六句自測，指出連專家都栽在同一個地方。頻率派的工具正確回答了一個定義清楚的問題，只是那個問題不是你想問的那個。

en.title: What a Confidence Interval Actually Is
en.subtitle: A poll's '±4 points', and the question of whom that 95% is really about
en.summary: A poll puts a candidate at 45% with a margin of error of ±4 points, and the paper writes that there is a 95% chance the true support lies between 41% and 49%. Almost everyone says this, and it is wrong. This piece derives a confidence interval by hand from a single mean, and watches the 95% lose its footing at the exact step where the observed numbers are plugged in. A submarine, a ratio interval, and a six-statement quiz then show that the experts fail at the same spot. The frequentist tool is not broken — it answers a well-defined question correctly. That question is just not the one you meant to ask.

articles.title: 為什麼叫虛無假設
articles.subtitle: 從一位喝茶的女士到一份聯署聲明：p 值爭議的觀念史
articles.summary: 「虛無」這個譯名，把 null 讀成了「什麼都沒發生」。Fisher 的 null 講的是可推翻性：實驗設下它，就是為了讓資料有東西可以反駁。這篇追一條線——品茶實驗如何生出第一個 p 值，Neyman 與 Pearson 如何把它改成一套決策規則，課本又如何把兩套邏輯焊成一個誰都沒設計過的東西，以及焊接處會裂在哪裡。

en.title: Why It Is Called the Null Hypothesis
en.subtitle: From a lady tasting tea to a signed statement: a short history of the p value quarrel
en.summary: Null was never about nothingness. Fisher's null is the hypothesis that can be nullified — set up so the data have something to argue against. This piece follows one line: how a tea party produced the first p value, how Neyman and Pearson turned it into a decision rule, how textbooks welded the two together into something neither man designed, and where that weld cracks.

articles.title: 大法官的差異有多大？
articles.subtitle: 用貝氏階層模型處理小樣本比例與部分匯聚
articles.summary: 甲在 4 件參與案件中提出 3 件個別意見書，乙在 100 件中提出 40 件。75% 與 40% 可以描述已觀察的案件，卻不足以支持排名。本文用二項模型、後驗分布與部分匯聚，說明小樣本比例應如何估計與報告。

en.title: How Large Are the Differences Between Justices?
en.subtitle: Small-sample proportions and partial pooling in a Bayesian hierarchical model
en.summary: Justice A files a separate opinion in 3 of 4 participating cases; justice B does so in 40 of 100. The two proportions describe the observed cases, but they do not justify a ranking. This article uses a binomial model, posterior distributions, and partial pooling to show how small-sample proportions can be estimated and reported.

glossaryGroups.label: 一次檢定的組成
glossaryGroups.blurb: 跑一次假設檢定會用到的基本概念：假設、分佈、機率、門檻。

en.label: What a test is made of
en.blurb: The basic ideas a hypothesis test is built from: the hypothesis, the distribution, the probability, the threshold.

glossaryGroups.label: 它會怎麼出錯
glossaryGroups.blurb: 同樣一套方法，用錯地方就給出錯的答案；這幾個詞講的是錯在哪、錯多少。

en.label: How it goes wrong
en.blurb: The same method gives wrong answers in the wrong places. These terms are about which way it fails, and by how much.

glossaryGroups.label: 誤用與它的後果
glossaryGroups.blurb: 研究者的實作習慣，如何把一套合理的方法變成大量製造假陽性的來源。

en.label: Misuse and its consequences
en.blurb: How ordinary research habits turn a reasonable method into a source of false positives.

glossaryGroups.label: 把行為估成位置
glossaryGroups.blurb: 看不到的立場、能力或傾向，怎麼從一格一格的投票或作答反推出來，還帶著它自己的不確定性。

en.label: Estimating positions from behavior
en.blurb: How an unobserved stance, ability, or leaning is recovered from a grid of votes or responses, carrying its own uncertainty.

glossaryGroups.label: 怎麼算是隨機了
glossaryGroups.blurb: 一個程序重複幾次，結果才能當成隨機的：距離怎麼定義，收斂是平滑的還是陡的。

en.label: When something counts as random
en.blurb: How many repetitions make an outcome random: how the distance is defined, and whether the approach is smooth or abrupt.

glossary.oneLine: 被設計來承受攻擊的那個假設：設下它，是為了讓資料有機會推翻它。

en.oneLine: The hypothesis set up to be attacked: it exists so the data have something to argue against.

glossary.oneLine: 同一個統計量在反覆抽樣下會長成的樣子。p 值與信賴區間都是從它身上量出來的。

en.oneLine: The shape a statistic takes under repeated sampling. Both p values and confidence intervals are read off it.

glossary.oneLine: 假設虛無為真，得到「像這樣或更極端」的結果的機率。

en.oneLine: The probability of a result at least as extreme as the one you got, if the null were true.

glossary.oneLine: 事前選定的門檻：長期而言，你願意讓多少比例的真虛無被錯判為顯著。

en.oneLine: A threshold fixed in advance: the share of true nulls you are willing to reject in the long run.

glossary.oneLine: 把標籤重新洗牌，看看純屬巧合能做到多好，再看真實資料排在哪裡。

en.oneLine: Shuffle the labels, see how well coincidence can do, then see where the real data land.

glossary.oneLine: 一套會生出區間的規則。95% 是這套規則的長期命中率，不是眼前這一個區間的機率。

en.oneLine: A rule for producing intervals. The 95% is the rule's long-run hit rate, not the probability for the one interval in front of you.

glossary.oneLine: 貝氏版的區間：在模型與先驗給定下，參數有 95% 的後驗機率落在這一段裡；正好是很多人誤以為信賴區間在說的那件事。

en.oneLine: The Bayesian interval: given the model and prior, the parameter has a 95% posterior probability of lying in this range. That is exactly what people wrongly believe a confidence interval reports.

glossary.oneLine: 先說清楚多大的差異才算重要，再用資料把效果關進這個範圍。

en.oneLine: State how large a difference would matter, then use the data to bound the effect inside that range.

glossary.oneLine: 兩種錯法：虛無為真卻拒絕它（誤報），虛無為假卻沒拒絕（漏抓）。

en.term: Type I and Type II error
en.oneLine: Two ways to be wrong: rejecting a true null (a false alarm), or failing to reject a false one (a miss).

glossary.oneLine: 效果真的存在時，這個研究抓得到它的機率。

en.oneLine: The probability that a study will catch an effect that is really there.

glossary.oneLine: 效果有多大，用一把不隨樣本數伸縮的尺量出來。

en.oneLine: How large the effect is, on a scale that does not stretch with the sample.

glossary.oneLine: 一邊看結果一邊調分析：多收幾個樣本、換個共變量、換個結果變數，直到 p 掉到門檻底下。

en.oneLine: Adjusting the analysis while watching the result — a few more subjects, another covariate, another outcome — until p drops below the line.

glossary.oneLine: 檢定做得夠多，光靠雜訊也會冒出「顯著」。不校正，門檻就名存實亡。

en.oneLine: Run enough tests and noise alone will hand you a "significant" one. Without correction the threshold means nothing.

glossary.oneLine: 在所有「顯著」的結果裡，真的有效果的佔幾成。它取決於這個領域有多少假說本來就是對的。

en.oneLine: Of everything that comes out "significant," how much is real. It depends on how many hypotheses in the field were true to begin with.

glossary.oneLine: 把 Fisher 的證據邏輯和 Neyman-Pearson 的決策邏輯焊成一套固定動作，兩邊的代價都不付。

en.oneLine: Fisher's evidential logic and Neyman-Pearson's decision logic welded into a fixed routine that pays neither one's price.

glossary.oneLine: 大量已發表的顯著結果，換一組人重做就做不出來。

en.oneLine: A large share of published significant findings do not come back when someone else runs the study again.

glossary.oneLine: 把每個投票者放到一條看不見的政策軸上，位置的選法要讓「誰跟誰投得像」被解釋得最好。這條軸是估出來的，不是先量好的。

en.oneLine: Each voter is placed on an unobserved policy axis, positioned so that who-votes-like-whom is explained as well as possible. The axis is estimated, not measured in advance.

glossary.oneLine: 把一副牌分成兩疊、讓兩疊交錯落下的洗法，也是撲克牌最常見的洗法。

en.oneLine: Splitting a deck into two packets and letting them fall interleaved, the way cards are usually shuffled.

glossary.oneLine: 兩個機率分佈之間，在同一個事件上機率差距的最大值。

en.oneLine: The largest gap between two probability distributions on any single event.

glossary.oneLine: 距離幾乎不動地貼著 1，到某個次數附近才在很短的區間內掉到接近 0。

en.oneLine: The distance sits at 1, then falls almost all the way to 0 within a short window around a critical number of steps.

glossary.oneLine: 一群人裡出現同一天生日的兩個人，需要的人數比直覺少得多：23 個人的機率就過一半。

en.oneLine: Fewer people than intuition suggests suffice for two of them to share a birthday: with 23 the odds already pass one half.
